chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Musa ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, who is Dawud ibn Farqad, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the sun sets, the time for Maghrib has entered, until the amount of time it takes for the pray-er to perform three raka'at passes. When that time has passed, the time for Maghrib and the last 'Isha has entered, until the amount of time it takes for the pray-er to perform four raka'at remains from the middle of the night. When that amount remains, the time for Maghrib has exited and the time for the last 'Isha remains until the middle of the night." As for that which indicates the consideration of the setting of the sun.
ai.seo_question: What are the exact start and end times for Maghrib and 'Isha prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates the Shia juristic principle of 'consideration' (i'tibar) for sunset as the definitive marker for Maghrib, while defining the end of the Maghrib window and the start of 'Isha al-Akhirah through a practical temporal calculation based on the duration of prayer. It reflects the scholarly consensus that the boundary between the two prayers is not a fixed astronomical event but a flexible interval determined by the time required to perform the respective rak'at, ensuring the validity of both prayers within their extended windows until the middle of the night.
